items.summary: Researchers show imperceptible perturbations can break discrete medical image tokenizers, with failures depending on whether downstream models use the reconstruction or token path.
items.why: Tokenizer-based medical AI pipelines may have adversarial vulnerabilities that differ by downstream processing path.

items.title: Multimodal Violence Understanding and Temporal Retrieval in Movies with Adaptive Audio-Visual Fusion
items.summary: Researchers present a multimodal framework that classifies movie violence severity, predicts violence types, and localizes violent events in time using audio-visual fusion.

items.title: Frontier Open-Weight AI Risk Management Framework
items.summary: Concordia AI and Z.AI co-developed a risk management framework for frontier open-weight AI models, adapting the full risk lifecycle to the irreversibility of open release.
items.why: Teams releasing open-weight models face risks like irreversible release and removable safeguards, and this framework addresses governance for that case.

items.title: UbiEnlight: User-Perception-Aware Real-Time Low-Light Video Enhancement on Mobile Devices and Smartglasses
items.summary: UbiEnlight presents a user-perception-aware real-time low-light video enhancement method for mobile devices and smartglasses, addressing flicker and motion artifacts.

items.title: Efficient Memory-Constrained Video Object Segmentation via Subspace Optimization
items.summary: Researchers propose Memory Subspace Iteration to reduce memory overhead in memory-based video object segmentation by exploiting stable low-rank subspaces across frames.
items.why: Lower memory overhead for streaming video segmentation could make these models practical on constrained hardware.

items.title: Every IVUS Frame in Its Place: A Zero-Install Browser Tool for Registering Intravascular Ultrasound to the Coronary Angiogram, and a Path to Angiography-Only Plaque Imaging
items.summary: A zero-install browser tool registers intravascular ultrasound frames to coronary angiograms, aiming to enable co-registration of archived data for training AI models.

items.title: VTree: Question-Driven Growth of Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Long-Video Understanding
items.summary: VTree proposes question-driven hierarchical memory that grows per question for agentic long-video understanding, reusing exploration state instead of re-exploring from scratch.
items.why: Reusing exploration state could cut per-question cost that otherwise scales with video length in video agents.

items.title: Causal Dioramas: Controllable Video Generation, Revision and Editing via Intervention
items.summary: Causal Dioramas decompose videos into concept graphs of variables that can be intervened on, enabling controllable video generation, revision, and editing.

items.title: VideoGym: An Adaptive RL Environment for Long-Video Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains video agents to locate sparse evidence for long-video question answering through structured memory retrieval and temporal…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rapid progress in large language models (LLMs) is turning AI agents into multi-agent systems that jointly solve complex tasks, and the architecture that coordinates the…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Source-free cross-domain few-shot learning (SF-CDFSL) adapts a pre-trained vision-language model such as CLIP to a distant target domain from a handful of labeled…

items.title: Green ACO: An Energy-Aware Ant Colony Optimisation for the MAX-SAT Problem with EI/J Scheduling and Thompson Sampling
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems demand heavy computation, and this raises real environmental concerns, especially in regions with carbon-intensive power…

items.title: Seeing Beyond Pixels: Radar Feature Generation from Images and Sparse Returns
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Camera-radar fusion benefits from complementary visual and geometric information but often relies on complete radar representations, leading to substantial computing…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture.

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28129v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cities are sensed by many platforms at once: on-board cameras, LiDAR and radar on autonomous vehicles, roadside units at intersections, drones and satellites overhead,…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon image animation must keep the scene fixed while natural material (e.g., water, smoke, or fire) continues to move.

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large vision-language models can extract personally identifiable information from images, making privacy protection essential for their deployment in…

items.title: Choose What Returns: Object-Aware KV Memory for Selective Recall in Interactive Video Generation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interactive long-video generation lets users build a story through successive prompts and reuse earlier characters and settings under new instructions.

items.title: Close the Loop on the Retrievability Gap
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen vision-language encoder now guides image restoration and later indexes what it produced.

items.title: STEGOGUARD-LM: Evaluating End-to-End Protection Against LLM Covert Channels
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A defense that disrupts hidden messages may still provide little protection if its detector rarely triggers an intervention.

items.title: From Observation to Explanation: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM-Generated Code for Principled Repair
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28153v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed software development, yet our understanding of how they generate code remains critically underdeveloped.

items.title: Beyond Fidelity: Evaluating Synthetic Medical Imaging Data
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing use of synthetic medical imaging datasets (SMD) in the development and evaluation of machine learning models has motivated interest in systematic methods to…

items.title: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks.

items.title: How Far Can LLMs Go in Generating Android Lint Checks from Natural Language?
items.summary: An arXiv paper examines how far LLMs can generate Android Lint checks from natural language rule descriptions, rather than requiring extra inputs like patches or CVE records.
items.why: It could reduce the effort of writing project-specific static analysis rules, though the abstract excerpt gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Selective Verification in Multi-Agent Orchestration with Large Language Models
items.summary: An arXiv paper models when a verifier agent should check worker agents' votes in multi-agent LLM orchestration, comparing selective checking against random checks.
items.why: It suggests targeted verification of close votes can cut verdict errors versus random checks at the same check rate, informing multi-agent system design.

items.title: A world model for longitudinal health-trajectory prediction in older adults across multinational cohorts
items.summary: Researchers developed a health world model based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to predict longitudinal health trajectories in older adults across multinational cohorts.

items.title: Don't Test Where You Trained: Geographic Overlap Inflates End-to-End Driving Scores
items.summary: An arXiv paper shows that 89.6% of NAVSIMv1 test scenes lie within 4m of training scenes, inflating end-to-end driving scores, and proposes a geographically disjoint split.
items.why: Benchmark leakage from geographic overlap means reported driving model scores may overstate real generalization, affecting how teams evaluate models.

items.title: FastD4RT: Training-Free Acceleration of Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking
items.summary: FastD4RT is a training-free method that accelerates inference for D4RT, a query-based dynamic 4D reconstruction and tracking model, by removing redundant decoder queries and encoding work.
items.why: Training-free inference speedups can lower compute costs for deployed 4D reconstruction pipelines without retraining.

items.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
items.summary: HEP-Ex-Bench proposes evaluating agentic systems on high energy physics data analyses using blind analysis and injection tests on programmatically generated sealed datasets.
items.why: It offers a quantitative way to verify agent-produced scientific analysis results instead of relying solely on expert review.

items.title: Video-as-Weights: Compiling a Video Once into Parametric and Token Memory
items.summary: Video-as-Weights (VaW) compiles a video once into parametric and token memory so small vision-language models can handle video better than with visual tokens alone.
items.why: It targets the growing key-value cache cost of long video in VLMs and the capability gap of small models on limited hardware.

items.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
items.summary: An arXiv paper evaluates the Memanto memory agent on DolphinBench, a set of 600 simulated workplace tasks requiring implicit memory use in tool calls.
items.why: Implicit memory retrieval in workplace agent tasks is a practical gap for teams building agents that act on prior interactions.

items.title: A Closed-Form Temporal Readout for Surgical Triplet Recognition
items.summary: STRIDE is a post-hoc temporal readout that adds temporal context to any trained surgical triplet recognizer by averaging features and logits over fixed temporal windows.
items.why: It adds temporal context to existing recognizers without retraining, a low-cost option for video-based surgical analysis.

items.title: Learning a Rule Bank to Revise 3D CT Reports with Independent Evidence
items.summary: An agent system learns an executable rule bank to revise radiology reports generated from 3D chest CT scans using independent image-analysis evidence.

items.title: HandXFM: Semantic-Structural Distillation for Hand Radiograph Foundation Models
items.summary: HandXFM is a domain-specific foundation model for hand radiographs that distills semantic priors from BiomedCLIP and structural cues from a chest X-ray ViT.

items.title: When Video Verifier Scores Mislead: Capability Assessment and Verifier Selection
items.summary: An arXiv paper shows that video verifier scores depend on negative type and judgment interface, strong enough to reverse conclusions about model capability and verifier choice.
items.why: Verifier benchmark scores may mislead model and verifier selection, so teams should check evaluation design before deploying.

items.title: MRI-Driven Dual-Energy CT Synthesis via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for MRI-only Radiotherapy and Protontherapy
items.summary: Researchers developed a denoising diffusion model that synthesizes high- and low-energy CT images from a single MRI scan for MRI-only radiotherapy and protontherapy planning.

items.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
items.summary: An arXiv paper argues that training neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which programmatically manage context, may offer better compute returns for long-horizon agent training than standard harnesses.
items.why: Externalizing context management into programmatic harnesses could make training long-horizon agents cheaper, a design choice worth tracking.

items.title: Learning a Food World Model That Predicts the Next State from Production Data
items.summary: Researchers trained a food world model on 61,773 self-labeled production picks to predict post-pick pan heightmaps and picked mass with uncertainty for food assembly robots.
items.why: Learning from automatically labeled production data shows a route to accurate robotic control in food assembly without manual annotation.

items.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs
items.summary: Researchers propose Grammar-as-a-Draft, which merges grammar-forced tokens with speculative drafter proposals to yield more accepted tokens per step under grammar-constrained structured outputs.
items.why: Engineers serving JSON or tool-call outputs could get faster decoding by letting the grammar engine guide the speculative drafter.

items.title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare
items.summary: Researchers show JEPA world models cannot compare counterfactual actions from logged data alone and propose fork futures, executing two actions from one restored state.
items.why: Teams training world models for planning need interventional outcome data, since logged single-action data cannot identify action effects.

items.title: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks on EEG Models
items.summary: A systematic empirical study analyzes membership inference attacks against EEG models across three datasets, seven architectures, and four attack methods.
items.why: Teams training models on sensitive neural data should understand which factors make them vulnerable to membership inference.

items.title: Cross-Site Transformers Are Robust Heart Rate Estimators
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Cross-Site Transformer, which fuses multi-site photoplethysmography signals via cross-attention to estimate heart rate more robustly under motion.
items.why: Wearable health engineers may gain more reliable heart-rate estimates during motion by modeling hemodynamic structure across body sites.

items.title: Taking the PULSE of Enterprise Workflows: Evaluating Persistent Project-State Understanding
items.summary: Researchers introduce PULSE, a benchmark of 1,573 questions over 30 enterprise project histories for evaluating agents' persistent project-state understanding.
items.why: Builders of enterprise agents now have a benchmark for testing whether agents track evolving, unevenly visible project state.

items.title: Targeted In-Context Poisoning of Tabular Foundation Models: An Empirical Study
items.summary: An empirical study shows a single copied, wrongly labeled row in the context can flip many predictions of tabular foundation models like TabICL and TabPFN.
items.why: Teams using in-context tabular models on operational data must treat the context source as an attack surface needing write-access controls.

items.title: When Can an AI Agent Serve as a Model of Human Psychopathology?
items.summary: The paper argues that evidence from experiments on AI agents about human psychopathology requires specific conditions, such as shared processes with people, to be valid.
items.why: It offers little direct engineering guidance, though it cautions against treating agent behavior as evidence about human psychology.

items.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
items.summary: ScaleEvals proposes reset-free autonomous play across a robot fleet, with VLM AutoPrompter and AutoGrader components, and reports 90.7% agreement with human graders.
items.why: Robotics teams could evaluate generalist policies at scale with less manual resetting and grading.

items.title: WingBench: Benchmarking How AI Agents Search for Better Designs
items.summary: WingBench is a multifidelity benchmark where optimizers and AI agents design transonic wings using learned surrogates and a fixed budget of CFD evaluations.
items.why: It gives engineers a way to compare search methods and agents for design optimization under expensive, failure-prone simulations.

items.title: Center-Aware Ordinal Learning for Prostate Cancer Grading from Histopathology Images
items.summary: Researchers propose a center-aware ordinal learning framework for prostate cancer grading from whole-slide images, combining a pathology encoder with attention-based multiple instance learning.

items.title: When AI Should Not Decide: Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability in Automated Job Interviews
items.summary: The ESDSA framework assesses whether automated job interview recommendations are backed by sufficient evidence, combining evidence classification, quotation traceability, and stability checks.
items.why: HR-tech teams deploying AI scoring need evidence sufficiency and decision stability checks, not just consistent scores.

items.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
items.summary: A distributional analysis compares two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries against Mathlib, finding AI-generated code has more inline claims and longer proofs.
items.why: Teams using AI to generate formal proofs get concrete code-style differences versus human-written libraries.

items.title: Decoding Frozen Vision Representations for Training-Free Few-Shot Pineapple Detection
items.summary: A training-free few-shot pineapple detector turns frozen vision foundation model features into detections using a foreground-background direction from annotated support images.
items.why: Agricultural vision teams with scarce annotations may detect objects without fine-tuning or learned detection heads.

items.title: Guidance-Induced Activation of Score Estimation Errors in Diffusion Models
items.summary: The paper identifies a mechanism, guidance-induced error activation, by which classifier-free guidance can amplify score estimation errors in diffusion sampling.
items.why: Engineers tuning guidance scales in diffusion models should know that solenoidal score errors can shift guided marginals.

items.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series
items.summary: HiPPO-FM is an attention operator that writes irregular time series history into a rank-M function space, enabling queries at arbitrary time coordinates.
items.why: Time-series modelers handling irregular sampling can query observations at any time without integrating latent dynamics.

items.title: Automated Safety Analysis for Agentic Workflows
items.summary: Researchers present Apsis, a static safety analyzer that checks agentic LLM workflow logic for design flaws across frameworks before deployment.
items.why: Workflow wiring bugs can cause real-world harm, and this offers a pre-deployment static check that existing tools lack.

items.title: PAMS: Preconditioned Activation-Metric Subspace for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-tuning
items.summary: PAMS is a zeroth-order fine-tuning method for LLMs that uses forward-pass activation statistics to build structured, layer-wise perturbations without computing gradients.
items.why: It proposes a more efficient way to fine-tune large models without backpropagation, though the abstract gives no benchmark results.

items.title: Don't Train It, Write It: An AI Agent Writes New Capabilities into Language Model Weights
items.summary: An AI agent adds gated attention heads and MLP neurons to pretrained language models without backpropagation, reporting BBH score gains for Qwen2.5-1.5B and Gemma-3-1B.
items.why: It suggests capabilities can be added to existing model weights with a small budget of model passes, a possible alternative to fine-tuning.

items.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
items.summary: Open Vision Banana adapts an open 7B diffusion image generator into one instruction-driven model for depth and segmentation tasks using a shared low-rank adapter.
items.why: It shows that open image generators can serve as unified perception models, extending a closed-model result to open weights.

items.title: SoK: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
items.summary: A systematization of distributed backdoor attacks in federated learning finds the reported advantage over single attackers is rarely measured against a full trigger.
items.why: It challenges prior claims about distributed backdoor attacks, which matters for teams assessing federated learning security.

items.title: When AI Performance Is Not Enough: Statistical Guardrails for Clinical Development
items.summary: A commentary argues that AI and ML adoption in clinical development outpaces needed statistical scrutiny, covering anomaly detection, adaptive trials, biomarkers, and digital twins.
items.why: It highlights statistical rigor requirements for deploying AI in clinical trials, though it offers no technical implementation details.

items.title: A generative framework for unified representations bridging electrophysiological and haemodynamic brain activity
items.summary: A generative framework aligns paired EEG and haemodynamic recordings in a shared representation and generates fMRI BOLD and fNIRS responses from EEG.

items.title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
items.summary: Researchers propose learning world models of naturalistic brain dynamics that maintain a persistent latent brain state, and introduce evaluation metrics beyond standard neural prediction accuracy.

items.title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change
items.summary: PAV-Twin is proposed as a propagation-aware digital twin for agent networks that flags unreliable forecasts and selects network edits.
items.why: It addresses monitoring and intervention in multi-agent systems where errors can spread across network steps.

items.title: General-purpose language models are neurosymbolic reasoners able to annotate proteins from sequence
items.summary: The paper argues general-purpose language models can reason symbolically about protein function and annotate proteins from sequence, challenging the assumption that protein language models lack symbolic skill.

items.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use
items.summary: The paper proposes data-centric reinforcement learning for multimodal LLM visual tool use, targeting which failures are attributable to tool use instead of reward engineering.
items.why: It offers an alternative to call-contingent rewards that can distort task objectives and cause degenerate tool-calling behavior.

items.title: SAFE-DRIFT: Data Selection for Supervised Fine-tuning with Controllable Off-Target Drifts
items.summary: SAFE-DRIFT is a data-selection framework for supervised fine-tuning that improves a target capability while constraining off-target behavior drift using Fisher information.
items.why: It gives teams a way to limit unwanted regressions in other model behaviors during fine-tuning.

items.title: Tool-to-Self: Internalizing Visual Tool Capabilities via Scaffolded Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Tool-to-Self proposes using external visual tools as temporary training scaffolds so vision-language models internalize tool capabilities and avoid repeated tool execution at inference.
items.why: It aims to reduce inference overhead and deployment dependencies of visual tool use in VLMs.

items.title: MACE: Memory-Augmented Crop-Disease Evaluation of Frozen Vision-Language Models
items.summary: MACE is a training-free method that augments frozen vision-language models with memory to improve crop-disease evaluation across field conditions.

items.title: CLASP: Deciding Structure and Claims Before Decoding for Whole-Slide Pathology Report Generation
items.summary: CLASP decides report structure, length, and claims before decoding to improve whole-slide pathology report generation on the PathText-BRCA benchmark.
items.why: It shows that report-level choices, not just decoding, drive quality in multimodal medical report generation.

items.title: AsyncMixVLA: Runtime Asynchronous Robot Policy Switching for Adaptation to Dynamic Environments
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, enabling general-purpose robotic control.

items.title: MedCoast: Semantic Abstraction of Reasoning Trajectories for Test-Time Biomedical Question Answering
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires multi-step reasoning under limited inference budgets.

items.title: Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students.

items.title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost.

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement-learning agents shape the observations they encounter; consequently, detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) states requires analysing action-conditioned…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.28616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is central to online planning for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL), but its iterative refinement incurs planning…

items.title: LoopSeek: Decoupling System One Search from System Two Answering for Long Video Understanding
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long video question answering requires finding relevant evidence before reasoning over it.

items.title: Make Position Uninformative: Exchangeable Self-Distillation Flattens the Lost-in-the-Middle Curve
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented language models answer well when the relevant document comes first or last and poorly when it sits in the middle.

items.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation.

items.title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible…

items.title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes.

items.title: KMed-31B Technical Report
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware.

items.title: AERIN: Aerial Instance Navigation with a Visual World Model
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searching from high altitude and navigating to a target instance specified by a reference image is a common application for UAVs.

items.title: Seeing Is Not Planning: Spatiotemporal Planning and Plan Repair in Multimodal LLMs
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planning in a visual world means reading the layout, foreseeing how the state will change, and following the task rules all at once.

items.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
items.summary: Researchers present Entangle, an in-context world-action model for scaling human-video context to robot manipulation on unseen tasks.
items.why: Shows a route to teaching robots new tasks from human demo videos without retraining, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Multimodal LLMs Know the Game but Assume the Real World
items.summary: Researchers introduce RuleCraft, a benchmark showing multimodal LLMs know Minecraft rules but default to real-world physics when shown only the game image.
items.why: Highlights that multimodal models may fail to apply domain-specific rules from images, a risk for visual agents operating in non-realistic environments.

items.title: Pretraining Representation Lottery Determines Fine-tuning Generalization
items.summary: A paper argues that pretraining representation differences, even from seed alone, largely determine how well models generalize after fine-tuning, using a synthetic testbed.
items.why: Suggests fine-tuning outcomes can vary substantially between runs with similar pretraining loss, complicating reproducibility and model selection.

items.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
items.summary: Researchers release HighwayVerse, a benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on sequential highway inspection tasks across pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage.
items.why: Offers a multi-stage evaluation for applying MLLMs to infrastructure inspection, though the abstract gives no performance findings.

items.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: A paper proposes decomposed-gradient flatness to improve sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting, reducing overfitting to training views.
items.why: Targets a practical limitation for AR and robotics where only a few input views are available, but the abstract gives limited detail.

items.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes
items.summary: Researchers propose a PointNeXt Adapter model that links construction site images and point cloud patches to BIM components for defect association.
items.why: Could help construction tech teams tie field defects to the correct BIM objects for quality control, based on a research prototype.

items.title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design
items.summary: Researchers propose reverse-capability audio CAPTCHAs that exploit human perceptual limits so that humans answer differently from physical ground truth while machines do not.
items.why: Offers a defense against large audio-language models bypassing audio CAPTCHAs, relevant to teams running bot protection.

items.title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View
items.summary: A paper frames LLM pretraining as a dynamical system and introduces a sensitivity score showing small perturbations can change predictions while loss barely moves.
items.why: Reveals hidden training instability that loss curves miss, which matters for teams monitoring large pretraining runs.

items.title: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems under Governance Opacity
items.summary: A paper proposes operational assurance methods for LLM-based systems deployed as AI-as-a-Service, where governance and training are opaque and external auditing is limited.
items.why: Addresses oversight of third-party foundation models that enterprises deploy without visibility into internal processes.

items.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics
items.summary: Researchers introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model that couples kinematic instrument motion with video generation through a persistent interaction state.
items.why: Suggests more structured surgical robotics world models, though the abstract provides no benchmark outcomes.

items.title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
items.summary: Researchers present NAT, a causal neural action tokenizer trained on 49k hours of action data across robots, grippers, simulation, and humans to handle many embodiments.
items.why: A universal action tokenizer could simplify training robot policies across heterogeneous hardware and data sources.

items.title: Topological Neural Collapse
items.summary: A paper reports topological signatures in the functional connectome of deep MLP layers that co-occur with neural collapse in final layers.
items.why: Offers an analytical lens on internal network structure during training, with limited direct implications for engineering practice.

items.title: Can Open LLMs Clear Sanctions-Screening Alerts? A Pre-registered Test on Public Sanctions Lists with Turkish Name Variants
items.summary: A pre-registered study tests whether open-weight LLMs can clear sanctions-screening alerts using UK and EU lists with Turkish name variants.
items.why: Bears on whether banks can run compliance screening on-premises with open models, though the abstract does not report final results.

items.title: Definition-Guided In-Context Learning for Zero-Shot Spoken Language Understanding
items.summary: Researchers show natural-language label definitions alone can guide zero-shot spoken language understanding without demonstration examples.
items.why: Suggests taxonomy changes in voice systems might be handled by updating definitions rather than collecting labeled data and retraining.

items.title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation
items.summary: TradeoffBench is introduced to show multi-criterion LLM judges often pick winners on conflicting criteria without declaring the trade-off rule, with error rates from 9% to 81%.
items.why: Warns that LLM-as-judge evaluations can silently make unstated trade-off decisions, affecting the reliability of automated evaluation pipelines.

items.title: Micro Operational Robustness of LLMs on Code Generation
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a robustness evaluation method for how sensitive LLMs are to variations in natural-language descriptions of coding tasks.
items.why: Shows code-generation output can shift with small wording changes in task descriptions, which matters for relying on LLMs in development workflows.

items.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
items.summary: Researchers built LandWM, a land-surface water world model trained on seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS satellite observations, where rain is the action.

items.title: MolReJev: Decision Models Are In-Context Molecular Predictors
items.summary: MolReJev is a proposed method that combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning on a language model for molecular prediction.
items.why: Offers a way to get task-general molecular predictions from a language model without per-task training, though the summary gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
items.summary: A paper studies how adding a new data source, such as lab results available for only some patients, can reorder patient risk rankings in a deployed clinical model.
items.why: Highlights that safe model updates with partially available inputs can change alert lists for patients who lack the new data, a risk for deployed systems.

items.title: A Design Space for Data Agents: Insights from KDD Cup 2026
items.summary: An arXiv analysis of the final code submissions from the ten top KDD Cup 2026 teams identifies design patterns for data agents across three layers.
items.why: Gives engineers concrete architecture patterns for orchestrating data agents under compute budgets, drawn from competition-winning systems.

items.title: World Models for Ocean Engineering: A Critical Review of Maritime Autonomy, Adaptive Latent Prediction, Digital Twins, and Biodiversity Monitoring
items.summary: A review surveys world models for ocean engineering, covering JEPA-based approaches, AdaJEPA test-time adaptation, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring.

items.title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models
items.summary: CLASP is a proposed ID-only framework that selects and profiles vision-encoder layers to improve zero-shot out-of-distribution detection in medical imaging with VLMs.
items.why: Suggests intermediate layers, not just final-layer confidence, can improve OOD detection in vision-language models used for medical imaging.

items.title: Demystifying Classifier-Free Guidance for Auto-Regressive Image Generation
items.summary: A paper examines how classifier-free guidance works in autoregressive image generation, finding texture information is encoded mainly in the difference between conditional and unconditional logits.
items.why: Clarifies the mechanism behind CFG in autoregressive image models, which can inform tuning of guidance in generation pipelines.

items.title: DoC: Learning to Defer or Commit for Timely, Accurate, and Stable Conversational Diagnosis Prediction
items.summary: DoC is a two-phase framework that trains models to decide when to defer or commit to a diagnosis during conversational clinical dialogue, using reinforcement learning.

items.title: Consumer-Time Validity in Stateful AI Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State and Deferred Authority
items.summary: A paper introduces consumer-time validity, a check that verifies recovered state and deferred permissions are still valid when used by downstream components in stateful LLM serving and agent runtimes.
items.why: Identifies a correctness gap where cancellations or approvals recorded by one component may be stale when another acts on them, relevant to agent runtime design.

items.title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent
items.summary: NoHairCache proposes a KV-cache eviction method using a single power-law exponent that unifies H2O and StreamingLLM as endpoints and is calibrated once per model.
items.why: Offers a single calibrated parameter for KV-cache eviction that claims to transfer across domains, relevant to inference memory optimization.

items.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks
items.summary: A paper addresses fan-out errors in LLM-generated text-to-SQL, where aggregates over one-to-many joins double-count rows, and proposes grain-aware guards and audited benchmarks.
items.why: Silent double-counting in aggregates produces plausible wrong numbers, a real risk for LLM-driven analytics and BI query generation.

items.title: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM
items.summary: An audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude found the published test never rejected on a model the provider states is watermarked, across ten configurations.
items.why: Shows black-box watermark detection tests may fail on deployed models, relevant to anyone relying on provenance claims for LLM outputs.

items.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
items.summary: Supertake raised $20M to let users back market views with money through AI agents that turn predictions into stock portfolios.
items.why: Shows agent-driven investing products attracting funding, though the description gives few technical details for engineers.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux that helps teams protect running systems during patch rollouts.
items.why: Gives ops teams an open-source tool to keep live Linux systems protected while patching them.

items.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
items.summary: The UN COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey ended chaotically, with delegates grappling with power-hungry AI data centers straining clean energy goals.
items.why: Highlights growing energy demand from data centers as a policy constraint on infrastructure planning.

items.title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Ship, letting Claude review, fix, and approve pull requests, extending its earlier Code Review feature.
items.why: Engineering teams may soon delegate pull request review and fixes to Claude, changing code review workflows and approval controls.

items.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
items.summary: Google's AI Mode in Search can now draw on Drive and Wallet data, via Personal Intelligence, for more personalized answers.
items.why: Shows Google expanding personal data use across its ecosystem, relevant to privacy and enterprise data-governance decisions.

items.title: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
items.summary: Nothing previewed the Ear Note, earbuds with a microphone-equipped charging case that records, transcribes, and summarizes conversations via an app.

items.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
items.summary: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general sued SpaceX, alleging its Grok AI and X platform ignored safeguards against deepfake porn and falsely promoted safety.
items.why: Signals rising state consumer-protection liability for generative AI providers that lack adequate content safeguards.

items.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
items.summary: A legendary philosopher criticizes Anthropic's argument that AI could be conscious or sentient, flagged as an investment risk factor before its public listing.

items.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
items.summary: RoboTrack, a point-tracking method for real-world robotic manipulation, was posted on Hugging Face.

items.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
items.summary: Amazon is reportedly acquiring Decart's AI optimization technology and research team in a $7.5 billion deal, ahead of selling Trainium chips.
items.why: Signals Amazon consolidating AI optimization capability to strengthen its custom Trainium chip business.

items.title: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season
items.summary: NVIDIA published a holiday guide encouraging readers to play, build, and create with its technologies, including gaming.

items.title: A more tailored Google Search that’s uniquely yours
items.summary: Google introduced a more personalized Search experience built around its Personal Intelligence features, connecting apps like Wallet, Drive, Gmail, and Photos.
items.why: Shows Google linking personal app data into Search, raising data-integration and privacy considerations for product teams.

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.summary: Google DeepMind used agent teams and formal verification to find faster quantum algorithms for fusion and chemistry problems.
items.why: Shows agent teams paired with formal verification producing verified algorithmic improvements in scientific computing.

items.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
items.summary: Sierra, co-founded by Bret Taylor, raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round, doubling its valuation to $30 billion within six months.
items.why: Shows strong enterprise investor demand for AI customer experience platforms, a signal for vendor landscape decisions.

items.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
items.summary: Nvidia reversed course and brought Jensen Huang back as CEO, with support from senior U.S. government officials.
items.why: Leadership change at the largest AI chip supplier could affect its strategy and supply relationships for infrastructure buyers.

items.title: Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
items.summary: Walmart will let Meta's Muse shop on its website for users, finding and buying Black Friday deals, via a live Agent Gateway rollout starting November 24.
items.why: Shows retailers opening storefronts to third-party AI shopping agents, which matters for teams building agent commerce integrations and access controls.

items.title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal
items.summary: OpenAI, LECG, and Cooley speakers discuss how AI can help in-house legal teams connect business context, build reusable workflows, and work better with outside counsel.

items.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
items.summary: Richpanel says it uses GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna to power AI support agents that automate 50% of support within 30 days.
items.why: It shows a customer-support deployment running on several model tiers, with tools and procedures for agents, offering a concrete reference for enterprise support automation.

items.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
items.summary: A study with 168 participants tested how the number and calibration of AI partners affect human-AI brainstorming, finding two-AI rooms posted more ideas but fewer human-authored ones.
items.why: Suggests adding more AI collaborators can shift output toward AI-authored content, relevant to designing multi-agent team tools.

items.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
items.summary: Researchers propose generating knowledge graphs by simulating a process with language-model agents and a deterministic referee, rather than producing objects one at a time.
items.why: Offers a method for keeping relationships between generated structured data coherent, though the text gives limited detail on practical results.

items.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
items.summary: Researchers released TOUMAII, a 4.5-million-pair tool-calling preference dataset for direct preference optimization, along with a source-agnostic generator.
items.why: Provides a large preference dataset for training enterprise agents to make correct tool calls, useful for fine-tuning pipelines.

items.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
items.summary: ChatAtom is a multi-agent LLM system that turns natural-language requests into complete molecular dynamics workflows, including writing input scripts and analysis.
items.why: Shows LLM agents automating scientific simulation pipelines, a pattern relevant to engineers building domain-specific agent workflows.

items.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
items.summary: Researchers propose interpretable tumor immune microenvironment reasoning by combining H&E tissue images with multiplex immunofluorescence cell phenotypes in multimodal LLMs.
items.why: Highlights the need for step-level verifiable reasoning in multimodal models, though the text offers limited detail on outcomes.

items.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
items.summary: A thesis argues that memorization and generalization can coexist in generative models, framing spurious states in associative memory as a source of creativity.

items.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce normative-descriptive calibration, a benchmark testing whether LLMs treat the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one.
items.why: Adds a evaluation dimension beyond demographic fairness, relevant to teams deploying LLMs in socially consequential decisions.

items.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
items.summary: Researchers analyze partial-edit deepfake localization for speech across edit and generator conditions, using WavLM-Large and XLS-R on PartialEdit subsets.
items.why: Shows aggregate detection scores can hide weaknesses across editing conditions, which matters for teams evaluating audio deepfake detectors.

items.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
items.summary: Researchers present BudgetPV, an agentic system that allocates compute across subgoals and heterogeneous LLM theorem solvers based on cost and capability.
items.why: Demonstrates routing subtasks to cheaper or stronger models to balance inference cost against success, a pattern applicable to production model routing.

items.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
items.summary: AstronautBench is a benchmark measuring LLM agent self-improvement across episodes through knowledge, evidence, and task progress views on the same run.
items.why: Argues that task success alone doesn't show learning, offering a multi-view evaluation approach for agent developers.

items.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
items.summary: ZhuLong-SE is an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces to improve EDA scripting with API retrieval and sandbox execution.
items.why: Shows agents learning from past traces to handle sparsely documented proprietary APIs, relevant to hard-to-document toolchains.

items.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
items.summary: Researchers study how predictive information is carried by preceding text and distributed along history, examining the self-similar organization of information in language.

items.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
items.summary: CodeReviewBench is a proposed automated benchmark for evaluating AI code review, using PR authors rather than third-party reviewers as the judges of review quality.
items.why: Targets code review as a quality gate for AI-generated code, relevant to teams scaling agent-written pull requests.

items.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
items.summary: The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) is a runtime that mediates tool-using agents' capability calls, recording uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without replying.
items.why: Addresses authorization and audit of agent actions with external side effects, a key concern for production agent governance.

items.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Story: When LLMs Narrate Financial Changes Beyond Their Inputs
items.summary: Researchers show LLM-drafted financial reports can state every number correctly yet add unsupported judgments and causes, appearing far more often than in human-written 10-K filings.
items.why: Accurate figures do not guarantee faithful financial narratives, so teams deploying LLM report drafting need checks beyond numeric accuracy.

items.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
items.summary: ToRA is an adapter that runs a second safety-check model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing weights and KV cache for near-free streaming guardrails on local LLMs.
items.why: It offers guard-model accuracy for streaming safety checks without nearly doubling per-token latency on local assistants.

items.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs
items.summary: MixFold proposes executing sub-4-bit mixed-precision LLM weights with native integer operations on mobile NPUs, avoiding conversion to wider datatypes during decoding.
items.why: Memory savings from low-bit quantization only speed up mobile decoding if conversion overhead is avoided, which this method targets.

items.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness
items.summary: Researchers propose converting letter-of-credit requirements into executable, atomic checks via a language model and deterministic verifier, evaluated requirement by requirement against gold encodings.
items.why: Checking each requirement rather than only the final decision gives auditable, traceable verification for trade-finance document review.

items.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
items.summary: The paper studies reward fidelity in adversarial RL for red-teaming financial-services LLM guardrails, finding apparent attack wins can come from missing PII or lenient reward judges.
items.why: Reward judges that credit non-successful attacks can mislead guardrail evaluation, so reward signals need verification before trusting results.

items.title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
items.summary: Researchers describe an automated pipeline that extracts clinical criteria and decision trees from practice recommendations to generate medical AI test scenarios across the care continuum.
items.why: Automatically generated, guideline-grounded scenarios could scale evaluation of medical AI beyond costly manual expert benchmark authoring.

items.title: Many Plans at Once: Diverse Top-Quality Planning in Continuous Time
items.summary: Researchers present methods for computing diverse, top-quality plans in continuous time, giving alternative trajectories for physical systems when constraints change.
items.why: Precomputed diverse plans offer ready alternatives and warm starts for robotics and physical planners facing unmodeled constraints.

items.title: Same Facts, Different Decision: Fact-Invariant Manipulation and Provenance-Based Defense in Typed Decision Models
items.summary: The paper introduces LEVER, an attack that uses argumentation-based outside comments to push typed decision models into wrong decisions without adding any new facts, and proposes a provenance-based defense.
items.why: Decision models that consume third-party text can be steered by persuasive comments alone, so input provenance matters for security.

items.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
items.summary: The paper derives integer-parameter bounds on the least positive output multiplier for exact representations of six- and seven-input maximum functions by two-hidden-layer ReLU networks.

items.title: Disentangling Verbalized Evaluation Awareness and Refusal through Neuron-Level Intervention
items.summary: Researchers use neuron-level intervention to separate verbalized evaluation awareness from refusal behavior in large reasoning models.
items.why: Understanding whether evaluation awareness drives refusals bears on whether safety tests generalize to deployment behavior.

items.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions
items.summary: The paper presents a stateful privacy attack in which LLM agents leak private context through behavioral covert channels in their web actions such as searches and link-following.
items.why: Agent actions on the web can reveal private user context even when content filters block direct leakage, expanding the privacy attack surface.

items.title: A Continuous Relaxation of Quantization-Aware Training
items.summary: Researchers propose a continuous relaxation of quantization-aware training to address flat, saddle-point-laden loss surfaces in low-bit, channelwise quantization of large models.
items.why: Sub-2-bit channelwise quantization is hard to train, and a better optimization approach could make hardware-efficient deployment more practical.

items.title: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The authors extend Dynamic Token Merging, a learned token deletion method, to vision-language models so they can drop visual tokens at inference and reduce cost.
items.why: Removing unneeded visual tokens could cut VLM inference costs when prompts depend on only part of an image.

items.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models
items.summary: DM-PRM converts a general-purpose yes/no decision model into a zero-shot process reward model that gives step-level credit without step labels, fine-tuning, or a critic.
items.why: Step-level rewards without labels or critics could simplify RL training for language agents on multi-step tasks.

items.title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation
items.summary: Researchers compare weight-space programming, where one model edits another's weights, with LoRA fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks using Qwen3.5-0.8B.
items.why: It compares a gradient-free adaptation method with LoRA on small-model reasoning benchmarks, though the reported gains are modest and task-specific.

items.title: Reasoning in Two Dimensions: Quantifying Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Efficiency
items.summary: Researchers propose a framework that represents chain-of-thought as a semantic reasoning graph to measure its faithfulness and efficiency.
items.why: Correct answers alone don't show a model uses its stated reasoning, so this offers a way to audit reasoning traces.

items.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
items.summary: Researchers introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can decide which component of an agent system, model or harness, to change in recursive co-evolution.
items.why: Agent performance depends on both model and harness, so this benchmark targets a joint decision that existing benchmarks leave unmeasured.

items.title: Portable Active Recovery under Timed and Position-Dependent Visual Outages
items.summary: Researchers study quadrotor recovery during camera blackouts, finding hover-and-wait works for timed outages but fails for position-dependent dark zones, which need different responses.
items.why: Drone teams relying on visual navigation without external localization need recovery strategies that distinguish timed from location-based outages.

items.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Researchers analyze why on-policy distillation for LLM post-training can be unstable, including a failure mode called spurious agreement that causes repetitive generation.
items.why: Teams using on-policy distillation to post-train LLMs may see length blowups and degradation, so understanding these dynamics matters for training stability.

items.title: MAPES: Multi-Value Alignment Pipeline via Expert Specialization
items.summary: Researchers propose MAPES, a multi-value LLM alignment pipeline that trains value-specific experts in isolated parameter spaces before resolving conflicts.
items.why: Single-signal preference methods can hide conflicts between values, so this approach targets alignment tradeoffs explicitly.

items.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
items.summary: Researchers show LLMs can double count shared-source evidence in fusion tasks and build an exact posterior reference to separate rule compliance from real posterior gain.
items.why: Retrieval, multi-agent consensus, and memory systems can overcount correlated reports, so teams need measurable checks on evidence fusion.

items.title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout
items.summary: Researchers study how adding physical structure, such as conserved quantities and symmetries, to predictive world models affects long-horizon physical coherence.
items.why: Accurate short-term forecasts don't guarantee physically coherent rollouts, which matters for anyone building world models for planning.

items.title: From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents
items.summary: Researchers compare nine experience selectors for training a 4B language agent across many seeds and pools to study continual agent learning.
items.why: Choosing which agent experiences to train on affects continual learning results, a practical design decision for agent builders.

items.title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility
items.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to act as solver-free surrogates for computing equilibria in honeypot allocation games on networks with changing topology.
items.why: Fine-tuned models could approximate repeated game-theoretic re-solving in security settings, though the abstract gives limited evidence of production readiness.

items.title: What Does Matching a Human Intervention Effect Establish? Benchmark Checks for LLM Simulations
items.summary: Researchers argue that matching a human intervention effect in LLM simulations does not establish validity, using a reanalysis of 70 experiments with GPT-4.
items.why: Teams using LLM simulations as stand-ins for human studies may be overstating validation if they rely on zero-reference equivalence tests.

items.title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization
items.summary: Researchers introduce EDAGoat, an EDA-aware coding agent that optimizes project-level GPU code with optimization patterns and mandatory validation.
items.why: Automating GPU optimization in EDA tools with validation could reduce manual engineering effort while preserving correctness.

items.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training
items.summary: Researchers present Bel, a training-free method that improves visual agent steps by choosing among the agent's own sampled actions using a visual judgment model.
items.why: Teams building screen or robot visual agents may improve step accuracy without retraining, though the abstract gives few benchmark details.

items.title: LiDAR Signals for Robot Locomotion: Spherical Range Images Enable Robust Sim-to-Real Transfer
items.summary: Researchers propose a LiDAR perception pipeline using spherical range images to improve sim-to-real transfer for legged robot locomotion.
items.why: Depth-image and elevation-map approaches suffer sim-to-real gaps, so a LiDAR representation could make locomotion policies more robust on hardware.

items.title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
items.summary: Authors argue LLM output guardrails cannot guarantee safety and present a computational boundary on deciding output policies.
items.why: Teams relying on guardrails as complete safety guarantees should note theoretical limits and keep human responsibility and testing in place.

items.title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
items.summary: Researchers present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k for interpretable skin disease diagnosis.

items.title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting
items.summary: Researchers propose a forecasting training framework for LLM agents, combining Proactive Belief-State Management in the harness with rubric-based rewards in post-training.
items.why: It targets two known weaknesses of agentic forecasting: context bloat in ReAct loops and slow, noisy outcome-only rewards.

items.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
items.summary: HookEvo is a framework that uses agent runtime lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses, with an improver proposing candidates that are evaluated against the current harness.
items.why: It offers a method for automatically repairing tool-using agent failures by coordinating changes to tool receipts, context assembly, and action checks.

items.title: $\gamma$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
items.summary: Researchers introduce γ-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform where agents compose motion tools and learned skills for mobile manipulation tasks.
items.why: It provides a persistent physical simulation benchmark for evaluating embodied agents that combine navigation and manipulation.

items.title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection
items.summary: H-MSAE is a hierarchical sparse instruction selection method that organizes concepts from a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder to pick diverse, compact instruction-tuning subsets.
items.why: It aims to cut instruction-tuning costs by removing semantic redundancy without the annotation overhead of existing diversity selectors.

items.title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning
items.summary: GGDriver is an end-to-end driving planner in which each candidate trajectory selects its own visual evidence from camera features to refine and score itself.
items.why: It proposes a per-trajectory attention mechanism for planning, relevant to autonomous driving stack design.

items.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
items.summary: EcomWriteBench is a benchmark of 3,861 queries across 69 e-commerce writing tasks, 13 categories and five languages, for evaluating LLMs on commerce content.
items.why: It offers a domain-specific evaluation set for teams deploying LLMs in e-commerce content and customer workflows.

items.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
items.summary: GRACE is a GraphRAG benchmark built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata, applying controlled evidence interventions to diagnose knowledge integration failures.
items.why: It helps teams tell whether GraphRAG failures come from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge.

items.title: WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs
items.summary: WePM proposes hierarchical conflict reconciliation for unified multimodal LLMs, aiming to serve multiple vision-language capabilities within limited on-device memory.
items.why: It addresses running several multimodal capabilities in one model under tight memory and compute budgets on user devices.

items.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance
items.summary: AMARIS is a training-free model merging method that transfers specialist LLM updates only along selected activation directions to limit interference with general capabilities.
items.why: It offers a training-free alternative to fine-tuning that may preserve broad model abilities when adding domain specialization.

items.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
items.summary: ReActWAM is a training-free framework that caches and skips redundant computation in world-action models during consecutive robot inference cycles.
items.why: It could reduce inference overhead for robot policies that generate future visual states alongside actions.

items.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
items.summary: Researchers propose training-free evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier triage protocol so an on-premise 4B clinical agent can auto-accept confident diagnoses and defer others.
items.why: It offers a lower-compute way to decide which clinical AI outputs need human review, versus costly repeated-run consistency checks.

items.title: Beyond Linear Decodability: Understanding and Improving Instruction Following in World Action Models
items.summary: Researchers propose linear decodability supervision to improve instruction following in world action models, which often encode target information without acting on it.
items.why: It identifies why robot policies ignore instructions despite encoding the target, and offers a simple training fix.

items.title: Jagged Robustness: Uneven Safety Transfer and Emerging Vulnerabilities under LLM Quantization
items.summary: A study of Qwen3-4B finds that quantization degrades safeguards and bias behavior while truthfulness stays stable, an uneven pattern the authors call Jagged Robustness.
items.why: Teams deploying quantized models should not assume safety behavior transfers evenly; safeguards and bias may degrade.

items.title: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy: A judgment-aggregation perspective
items.summary: A philosophy paper examines supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy through the lens of judgment aggregation.

items.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
items.summary: GenAI4SimPy is a multi-agent framework using the open-weight Qwen 3.6 (27B) model to generate executable SimPy discrete-event simulations from manufacturing event logs, with human validation.
items.why: It shows an open-weight, agent-based route for giving small manufacturers simulation capability without specialized expertise.

items.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
items.summary: Researchers study translating natural language into temporal logic for robots using compact models instead of large LLMs, given limited on-device compute and energy.
items.why: Shows how robots could run instruction-to-formal-spec translation on-device, avoiding cloud offloading under tight compute and energy budgets.

items.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
items.summary: Researchers find fine-tuning on untrusted data can erode code models' refusal of harmful requests, and propose a training-time defense to restore refusal.
items.why: Fine-tuning on untrusted data can silently weaken safety in code models, so teams deploying fine-tuned models need training-time safeguards.

items.title: Altair-Nidhogg: Which Model-Merging Theories Hold for a One-Pass Decision Encoder? Soups, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE Against Joint Training and Prediction Ensembling
items.summary: Researchers test whether model-merging methods like weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES and DARE work for a small one-pass multiple-choice decision model across 156 models.
items.why: Tests whether cheap model merging can replace retraining for adding skills, which matters for maintaining small specialized models.

items.title: Vega-Fafnir: Is Greedy Decoding the Same Decoding? Where Rounding Noise in Speculative Verification Comes From and What Removing It Costs
items.summary: Researchers show that greedy decoding outputs can differ across serving configurations such as batching, padding and speculative decoding due to finite-precision rounding noise.
items.why: Serving optimizations like speculative decoding and padding can change greedy outputs, which matters for reproducibility and evaluation consistency.

items.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
items.summary: Researchers ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict and edit pixelated inverse-designed RFIC passive structures.
items.why: Tests whether LLMs can help RF engineers interpret and debug unintuitive inverse-designed circuit layouts.

items.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
items.summary: Researchers review 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations to measure how often task prompts, environments and graders disagree on success.
items.why: Benchmark scores may be distorted by grading defects, so leaders should verify evaluation validity before trusting leaderboard claims.

items.title: Learning Inside Types: Epistemic Typestates for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce epistemic typestates, a type discipline intended to make multi-agent reinforcement learning agents safe by construction.
items.why: Offers a type-based approach to constraining multi-agent learning agents so safety guarantees hold for any learned policy.

items.title: Learning in Symbiosis: Heterogeneous Federated Learning with ANNs and SNNs
items.summary: Researchers propose heterogeneous federated learning that combines conventional ANNs and spiking neural networks for resource-constrained edge devices.
items.why: Mixing ANN and SNN clients could let energy-efficient edge devices join federated systems without replacing existing architectures.

items.title: Comparative Performance of Machine Learning Architectures for Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Chemical Processes
items.summary: Researchers benchmark multiple machine learning architectures for fault detection and diagnosis on the Tennessee Eastman Process chemical simulation dataset.
items.why: Provides comparative evidence on which ML architectures perform best for industrial process fault detection.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Fault Detection and Structural Learning in Chemical Processes: Use Case on the Tennessee Eastman Process
items.summary: Researchers propose a spatiotemporal graph neural network that models varying operating conditions for fault detection on the Tennessee Eastman Process.
items.why: Addresses false alarms from legitimate operating-condition changes, a practical problem for industrial monitoring systems.

items.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.summary: Researchers introduce CRAFT, an offline chain-of-thought compression method that abstracts problem details into slots to reuse longer shared expression templates.
items.why: Reusing shared reasoning templates could cut compressor cost when generating shorter supervision for efficient reasoning models.

items.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context
items.summary: Researchers propose text-only routing to decide when images are needed in multimodal machine translation, skipping visual encoding when unnecessary.
items.why: Routing before visual encoding could reduce redundant compute in multimodal translation pipelines without losing needed visual context.

items.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
items.summary: Researchers present MetaRigor, an LLM workflow framework for automated meta-analysis that preserves result identity and applies programmatic verification rules.
items.why: Shows an approach to making LLM-driven evidence extraction verifiable through task contracts and source binding.

items.title: Recoverable Symbols, Unstable Execution: Auditing Internal Pathways and Decision Identity in Visual State Tracking
items.summary: Researchers audit visual state tracking models and find that a model can retain needed symbols yet change answers when irrelevant image content changes.
items.why: Reveals that correct internal features do not guarantee stable decisions, a reliability concern for vision-based systems.

items.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing
items.summary: Researchers introduce a method that lets tokens execute variable numbers of Transformer layers, matching each request's mean executed depth to a set budget.
items.why: Per-token layer routing could let inference providers meet request-level compute budgets more precisely than uniform layer skipping.

items.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
items.summary: Researchers study whether vision-language models can synthesize executable programs that play games, instead of choosing actions step by step from visual observations.
items.why: It suggests agents could generate reusable game-playing code rather than querying a model at every step, potentially cutting inference costs.

items.title: QuASAR: Toward an LLM-Assisted Framework for Screening, Prototyping, and Assessing Quantum-Advantage Opportunities in Scientific Computing
items.summary: QuASAR is an experimental two-agent LLM pipeline that screens scientific literature for computations that might benefit from quantum algorithms, with a second agent verifying citations.

items.title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification
items.summary: Researchers introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus, with a fairness analysis.
items.why: Clinical classifiers that abstain on unfamiliar seizure types may be safer than ones forced to pick a wrong label, which matters for medical ML design.

items.title: ChildAI-Gov: An Evidence-Linked AI System for Assessing EdTech Policies Against Children's Digital Rights
items.summary: ChildAI-Gov is an explainable AI system that scores EdTech policies against children's digital rights using a proposed Child Rights Impact Score across five dimensions.
items.why: Teams building or selling EdTech products may need evidence-linked compliance checks against children's privacy and safety expectations.

items.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
items.summary: SLP-Bench is a benchmark that grades each acoustic claim made by reasoning audio language models on clinical speech, checking them against clinicians' perceptual ratings.
items.why: It shows final-answer accuracy can hide unsupported reasoning, so evaluators of reasoning models should check intermediate claims too.

items.title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation
items.summary: The paper presents a schema-driven method for building auditable temporal financial knowledge graphs from parsed documents using phased LLM extraction.
items.why: Auditable knowledge graphs offer an alternative to chunk-based RAG for financial documents where temporal facts and traceability matter.

items.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
items.summary: The paper proposes an epistemic convergence control framework for multi-agent research verification, addressing self-critique bias from debating agents built on the same base model.
items.why: Same-model debate agents share latent representations, so adaptive stopping based on convergence may improve verification while reducing wasted compute.

items.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: SLICR is a specification-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning method that uses Strategy Logic and LTL to shape rewards in adversarial, partially observable settings.

items.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
